lines.t: Every idle word, rising in the air,
Scoffing at the warning, mocking what is fair.
Tongues like sharpened arrows, laughing at Your call,
Building up a tower that’s destined still to fall.
They say, “Where is His promise? Where is now His hand?”
They trample on the holy, they love the shifting sand.
They speak against Your counsel, they call the truth a lie,
Forgetting every whisper that nothing escapes Your eye.
Every idle word will stand in the fire,
Every careless breath will rise ever higher.
All the bitter mocking, every hardened sound,
Will echo back in judgment when Your voice comes down.
Teach my lips to tremble at the things I say,
Let my heart speak only what will not burn away.
Some say, “Who can hear Him? Who knows what He has spoken?”
They jest at all Your mercy, they treat Your love as broken.
They drag Your name through darkness, for gain and for applause,
Blind to the coming moment when You will plead Your cause.
But You weigh every sentence, every seed of speech,
You hear what the tongue sows in the hidden reach.
For words are like a river, flowing from the heart,
Revealing what is living, and what has grown apart.
Every idle word will stand in the fire,
Every careless breath will rise ever higher.
All the bitter mocking, every hardened sound,
Will echo back in judgment when Your voice comes down.
Wash my lips with coal from the altar flame,
Let my mouth bear witness to Your holy name.
Let no idle whisper curse the things You’ve done,
Let no scoffer’s laughter drown the voice of Your Son.
Break the proud defiance, silence every lie,
Call the mocker to repentance before the day is nigh.
Turn our idle chatter into honest prayer,
Turn our empty thunder into truth laid bare.
So I lay down my phrases, the careless and untrue,
The jokes that pierced my neighbor, the doubts that spoke of You.
I turn from every murmur that loved the world’s reward,
I choose the narrow language that honors The Lord.
Every idle word will stand in the fire,
But a humbled tongue is all that You desire.
Fill my mouth with mercy, let my speech be clean,
A witness to Your glory in all that’s heard and seen.
On that coming morning, when all hearts are stirred,
Let me stand forgiven for every idle word.
Guard the gate of my lips, keep my spirit stirred,
Till every breath that leaves me is a faithful word.
